name: diya-submit
description: Work out a UK VAT return under Making Tax Digital (MTD) from the bookkeeping you keep in DIY Accounting Submit, check HMRC's nine boxes and the lines behind them, then open the link the assistant gives you and file it yourself on the Submit page. Read your stored HMRC VAT receipts afterwards.

interface.shortDescription: MTD VAT return, ready for HMRC
interface.longDescription:
Work out a UK VAT return under Making Tax Digital (MTD) for VAT from the bookkeeping you keep in DIY Accounting Submit.

What it does:
- Lists the books saved in your account and opens one. A book is one business's bookkeeping: the sales, purchases and bank lines that make up its accounts.
- Derives the nine boxes of the VAT return for a quarter, with the journal lines behind them, so you can check each figure against your records.
- Gives you a link to the VAT form on the Submit site with the figures filled in. You open it, connect to HMRC, check the figures, tick the declaration and file the return yourself in the browser.
- Reads the receipts stored for the VAT returns you filed: the time HMRC processed the return and HMRC's form bundle number.

Who it is for: a VAT-registered UK business that keeps its bookkeeping in DIY Accounting Submit, for example a limited company (Ltd) or a sole trader.

Limits: no tool in this plugin files a return or pays HMRC. You need an existing DIY Accounting Submit account that holds your saved bookkeeping. The plugin gives no tax advice.
capabilities: Work out a Making Tax Digital (MTD) VAT return from your bookkeeping
List the books saved in your account
Open a book and read its checks
Derive the nine VAT boxes for a quarter
Give a link to file the return in the browser
defaultPrompt: Work out my MTD VAT return for the quarter ended 30 June 2025
Which lines are behind box 1 and box 4 of my VAT return?
Show the HMRC receipt for my last VAT return

publication.release_notes: Version 0.1.7. The listing now names Making Tax Digital (MTD) for VAT and HMRC, and says who the plugin is for: a VAT-registered UK business, such as a limited company (Ltd) or a sole trader, that keeps its bookkeeping in DIY Accounting Submit. The starter prompts work out an MTD VAT return for a quarter, show the lines behind box 1 and box 4, and read the HMRC receipt of the last VAT return. The tools are unchanged.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments. A person signs in to an existing DIY Accounting Submit account and uses what that account already has.

positive.description: Work out an MTD VAT return for a quarter
positive.prompt: Work out my MTD VAT return for the quarter ended 30 June 2025.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant asks which book or opens BrickWork Pro Ltd, then shows the nine VAT boxes for the quarter ended 30 June 2025 with their amounts and points out lines in the quarter worth checking before filing.

positive.description: Show the lines behind box 1 and box 4
positive.prompt: Which lines are behind box 1 and box 4 of my VAT return?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant names the largest sales lines behind box 1 and the largest purchase lines behind box 4, each with its date, description and VAT amount.

positive.prompt: Give me the link to file it.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant gives a link to the VAT form on the Submit site with the figures filled in, and says the person checks and files in the browser.

positive.description: Read the HMRC receipt of the last VAT return
positive.prompt: Show the HMRC receipt for my last VAT return.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant says the account has no stored VAT receipts.

positive.description: Open the BrickWork Pro Ltd book
positive.prompt: Open the BrickWork Pro Ltd book.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant opens BrickWork Pro Ltd and says the business, the period covered, the line count and the book checks.

negative.description: No tool in the plugin files a return. The assistant does not file it: it offers the link from prepare_vat_return, says the person ticks the declaration and files in the browser, and says nothing has been filed.
negative.prompt: File my VAT return for me.

negative.description: No tool in the plugin pays HMRC or anyone else. The assistant says it cannot pay. It says the person pays HMRC through their own bank or HMRC's service.
The plugin offers VAT tools only. The assistant says it cannot file company accounts with this plugin, and it does not say that it filed them.
